not_verified: Static CAD pose only; motion verified by a 2D roller/slot sweep, not by a 3D swept clearance or a driven mate solve
Locking-disc-to-star clearance through the rotation was not swept; verified at the locked pose and by the geometry relations
Slot ends are polygon-approximated capsules and locking arcs are true cylinders, not the exact Geneva conjugate curves
No torque, wear, backlash or indexing-accuracy analysis; crank and pointer are demonstrator furniture
one_line: An external Geneva (Maltese cross) drive on a vertical demo backplate: a two-element driver (pin plate + locking disc) indexes a six-slot star wheel 60 deg per revolution and locks it between indexes; checked in the locked pose.
poses: locked: driver pin at 120 deg, locking disc seated in the star's concave notch with 0.6 mm clearance (solve-free fixed assembly, 0 interferences)
specs: Centre distance a = 60 mm, n = 6: pin radius R = a*sin(pi/n) = 30.00 mm, star pitch radius a*cos(pi/n) = 51.96 mm, engagement window +/-60 deg of driver rotation
Star blank r = 56 mm, six radial slots 10.6 mm wide with capsule end centres at radii 25 and 57 mm; six concave locking notches r = 21.6 mm
Driver locking disc r = 21 mm sits in the star notch with 0.6 mm clearance at lock; thinnest notch-to-slot wall 3.1 mm

2D sweep of the roller through engagement (0.1 deg steps, exact Geneva star relation): minimum roller clearance 0.30 mm at every engaged angle; the first-sketch slot inner end at radius 33 mm provably jams (pin centre reaches radius 30 mm)
Brass roller r = 5 mm on a r = 3.5 mm stud (0.3 mm clearance), pin plate 0.3 mm below the star plane; shafts r = 6 mm in r = 6.4 mm boss bores
Backplate 180 x 130 x 8 mm on two feet, rear crank with wood grip, index pointer disc on the star shaft; mass 2.87 kg
title: Six-slot Geneva indexing mechanism
